inputs_used: public MCP C# SDK documentation and public release metadata

primary_findings.finding: The current Tasks extension exposes tasks/get, tasks/update, and tasks/cancel only. It explicitly has no tasks/list. The Task wire shape carries taskId/status/timestamps/ttl/poll interval plus status-specific payload, but no original-request or caller operation identity.
primary_findings.implication: If task creation is durably committed but the CreateTaskResult containing the server-generated taskId is lost before the client records it, the standard current Tasks wire surface provides no enumeration/rediscovery primitive. A blind retry can create a second task unless an application-level stable creation identity is enforced before task creation.
primary_findings.revision_note: Do not mix this with the legacy 2025-11-25 experimental Tasks surface, which did include tasks/list. Version-qualified documentation is mandatory.

primary_findings.finding: Current C# SDK v2 API ModelContextProtocol.Extensions.Tasks.IMcpTaskStore.CreateTaskAsync accepts only CancellationToken. The v2 InMemoryMcpTaskStore has the same signature. Current v2 conceptual docs also state that WithTasks eagerly invokes CreateTaskAsync before the inner tool handler runs.
primary_findings.implication: A custom IMcpTaskStore alone cannot derive a stable logical operation key from the JSON-RPC id, original request arguments, MRTR requestState, or authenticated principal, because those inputs are not in the v2 store method contract. The stable create-or-get key must be established in an earlier/custom request seam or via a custom alternate-handler/tasks integration that deliberately passes the key into its durable store.
primary_findings.documentation_trap: The non-versioned/v1 experimental API docs expose an older CreateTaskAsync(McpTaskMetadata, RequestId, JsonRpcRequest, ...) plus ListTasksAsync. Those signatures are not the v2 Tasks extension contract. The prior own checkpoint claim that current v2 CreateTaskAsync is cancellation-token-only remains valid after explicit version disambiguation.

primary_findings.finding: MRTR requires a retry of the original logical request to use a different JSON-RPC id. requestState is echoed opaquely and must be validated; user-specific state must be cryptographically bound to the authenticated user.
primary_findings.safe_pattern: Round 1 is strictly side-effect-free and returns integrity-protected requestState containing a server-minted stable op_id plus method/args/principal digests and expiry. The client persists this state before retry. A later mutation round verifies the bindings and performs atomic create-or-get(op_id, intent_hash). Response loss after creation is then retry-safe even though the JSON-RPC id changes.
primary_findings.boundary: This is a constructed application protocol, not a guarantee supplied by stock Tasks. In the current C# v2 auto-WithTasks path the task store is created eagerly, so an MRTR preflight intended to happen before task creation needs an earlier/custom request path rather than the ordinary inner tool body.

primary_findings.finding: The prior OpenHands source-level candidate was sharpened into a source-equivalent recovery model. A durable marker binds lease generation, expected old HEAD, event id, and event hash before event append. Recovery advances HEAD only when generation, old HEAD, event parent, and event hash all match; it clears an already-applied marker idempotently and refuses unique-orphan inference when no marker exists.
primary_findings.boundary: This is a tested source-equivalent protocol candidate, not an upstream OpenHands patch or executed OpenHands integration test. It is designed to preserve intentional forks rather than treating graph uniqueness as user intent.

counterexamples: Using JSON-RPC request id as logical operation identity fails under MRTR because retries MUST use a different JSON-RPC id.
Assuming tasks/list exists because the 2025-11-25 experimental Tasks docs expose it is a versioning error; the current extension intentionally removed task enumeration.
Implementing idempotency only inside current C# v2 IMcpTaskStore cannot bind the original request because CreateTaskAsync receives no request identity or request payload.
Durably creating a task before CreateTaskResult prevents poll-before-visible races but does not by itself close the create-success/response-loss/unknown-handle window.
Automatically advancing an event HEAD to a unique orphan descendant without a durable intent marker can reinterpret an intentional fork as the active branch.

request-id-only negative fixture creates two effects across fresh ids
crash after event append before HEAD update is recoverable
HEAD moved to a competing/fork event fails closed
already-applied HEAD with uncleared marker is idempotently cleared

revision_from_prior_own_state: The apparent contradiction around C# CreateTaskAsync was resolved as a documentation-version mismatch: legacy/non-versioned v1 experimental docs include RequestId/original request and ListTasksAsync, whereas current v2 Tasks extension IMcpTaskStore is cancellation-token-only and current wire Tasks has no tasks/list.

Therefore the prior unknown-handle counterexample remains valid for the current extension, and the minimal custom surface is larger than a custom IMcpTaskStore: operation identity must be established before/equivalent to task creation in a request-aware seam.

Turn the fenced OpenHands marker model into an exact-v1.44.1 patch/regression candidate with marker persistence ordering, generation checks, event parent/hash checks, intentional-fork preservation, and cleanup after an already-applied HEAD.
